title: Cust VPC Change Simulator and Sample Audit Corpus
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working PRD / engineering sketch for a lightweight customer VPC change simulator and a curated sample audit corpus intended to: (1) exercise our approval gate logic, sampling and retention heuristics, and attestation bundling; (2) validate telemetry shape and queryability for forensic playback; (3) produce realistic rejection/rollback/rollback-recovery scenarios for SRE and support drills.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Customers performing private deployments manage their own networks and will occasionally make configuration changes (SG, route, peering, NAT). These changes must flow through our approval gates or be captured fully in audit evidence when done out-of-band.
- We need a reproducible test harness that can generate varied, realistic change traces (benign changes, configuration drift, misapplied firewall rules, partial peering failures) and an associated audit corpus that represents evidence bundles (logs, netflow, sha-signed change manifests).
- Current PRDs focus on policy and retention; we lack a repeatable way to validate operator experience, failure modes, and query patterns for downstream tooling (search, timeline, forensics).

Goals (what success looks like):
- Deliver a CLI-driven simulator that can synthesize change events with parameters (change_type, scope, operator_role, approval_path, evidence_quality).
- Produce a set of 120 sample audit bundles across 6 classes (approved, auto-approved, rejected, emergency-bypass, partial-apply, rollback) that cover our expected query surface (by tenant, by operator, by timeframe, by change hash).
- Ensure each bundle contains a compact set of artifacts: change-manifest.json, operator-assertion.sig (simulated HSM signature), agent-syslog tail, network-trace (pcap-lite), and a compact summary.json with canonical fields for quick indexing.
- Define compatibility tests for Console playback, SIEM-forwarder ingestion, and on-prem observability export.

Non-Goals:
- This project will not implement a hardened HSM signing pipeline — signatures are simulated but schema-compatible with future KMS-backed receipts.
- We are not building a full traffic generator; pcap-lite will be synthetic, small, and focused on metadata that our parsers exercise.

Key definitions and canonical fields (summary.json schema):
- tenant_id: string (redwood tenant namespace id)
- change_id: string (uuid v4)
- change_type: string (route_update | security_group_update | peering_add | peering_remove | nat_delta)
- operator: string (email)
- operator_role: string (tenant-admin | delegated-operator | support-bridge)
- request_time: iso8601
- approval_path: string (console-canary | api-reserved | delegated-approval | emergency-bypass)
- approval_result: string (approved | rejected | timed_out | bypassed)
- manifest_hash: sha256
- evidence_quality: string (complete | partial | truncated)
- forensic_tags: list of short strings (we will store as comma-separated string in the corpus)

Simulator design (CLI + engine):
- Entry: rd-vpc-simulate run --profile PROFILE --seed SEED --count N --outdir /tmp/corpus
- Profiles (examples):
  - small-change-fast: single SG rule add, operator role delegated-operator, expected approval path console-canary
  - cross-region-peering-failure: peering_add with simulated partial propagation and route-ads update; evidence_quality=partial
  - emergency-rollback: nat_delta that triggers emergency-bypass; approval_result=bypassed, with post-facto attestation bundle
- Engine components:
  - event-synthesizer: creates change-manifest.json and deterministic operator actions from seed
  - evidence-generator: emits artifacts (syslog snippets, pcap-lite, manifest.sig) and synthesizes manifest_hash
  - timeline-builder: produces chronological event stream (request -> approval request -> approval decision -> apply steps -> monitoring alerts -> rollback)
  - corpus-packager: zips each scenario into an evidence bundle and writes summary.json (index-friendly)

Sample audit bundle (human-readable example for review):
- summary.json
  {
    "tenant_id": "tenant-82f3",
    "change_id": "9f2c8b4a-3a1d-4e2e-9a0b-1111111",
    "change_type": "security_group_update",
    "operator": "ops+alice@acme.example",
    "operator_role": "delegated-operator",
    "request_time": "2024-10-28T18:22:40Z",
    "approval_path": "console-canary",
    "approval_result": "approved",
    "manifest_hash": "sha256:...",
    "evidence_quality": "complete",
    "forensic_tags": "sg-change,login-from-nonprod"
  }

(above is stored inside each bundle; real JSON in artifact file — here we show for reviewers)

Acceptance criteria for product and infra teams:
- Simulator binary (or Python script) runs in CI producing deterministic bundles when a seed is provided; artifacts are small (<5MB each bundle) and stored under s3://redwood-evidence-dev/sim-corpus/<release> for retrieval.
- Console can ingest a bundle and render a playback timeline (request -> approval -> apply -> alerts -> rollback) without schema changes to the Console timeline UI.
- SIEM-forwarder can index summary.json and extract manifest_hash, tenant_id, and approval_result into a test index.
- A small test harness exists that asserts queries: counts by approval_result, counts by operator_role, and latencies from request_time to approval decision.

Test matrix and scenarios (high level):
- Categories: approval_behaviour (approved/rejected/timeout/bypass), evidence_integrity (complete/partial/truncated), application_impact (no-service-impact, partial-failure, outage), operator_timeline (single-op, multi-op-handoff), scale (single change, bulk 50 changes).
- For each scenario we define EXPECTED_CONSOLE_STATE and EXPECTED_SIEM_EVENTS (documented in test matrix CSV in repo).

Operational considerations and retention experiments:
- Bundles will be compact (summary + minimal binary artifacts). We will evaluate retention and S3 cost for 6 months of generated corpus at scale 10k bundles/day.
- Propose a TTL experiment: store full bundles for 30 days, archive compact summary-only records for 365 days. Evaluate usefulness to support during a simulated incident.

Security and privacy notes:
- All simulator-generated tenant IDs and operator emails are synthetic and labeled "sim" to avoid accidental cross-contamination with customer data.
- Signature artifacts are simulated. Avoid using this simulator as a certifying tool; it is only for UX/telemetry/forensics testing.

Console / UX playback requirements (short):
- Timeline view should be able to accept a bundle endpoint (local file or s3 path) and step through events. Improve timeline to show "evidence_quality" indicator and link to artifacts (view syslog snippet, download pcap-lite).
- Provide a compact summary card in rollouts page that highlights approval_path and approval_result and links to bundle manifest_hash.

Open questions and decisions needed:
- Do we standardize the compact summary JSON schema now (breaking change for Console)? Proposal: adopt the schema above and version it as v1.0-summary. Decision due by 2024-12-05.
- Where to publish simulator artifacts for reuse? Proposal: s3://redwood-evidence-dev/sim-corpus/<branch> + a simple index endpoint maintained by infra.
- What are acceptable sizes for pcap-lite? Proposal: cap at 200KB per event to keep bundles small.

Implementation plan (quarterly roadmap):
- Week 1-2: prototype CLI and simple profile templates (Marcus, Jules)
- Week 3-4: produce first 30 bundles and run Console ingest smoke tests (Aisha, product)
- Week 5-6: integrate SIEM-forwarder test harness and prepare test matrix (Priya)
- Week 7-8: iterate on schema and produce acceptance test coverage in CI (all)

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: simulated evidence might accidentally differ from customer artifact shapes. Mitigation: collect anonymized example shapes from recent support tickets (security review) and incorporate into profile templates.
- Risk: corpus grows and costs escalate. Mitigation: TTL policy and compact-summary archival.

Next steps / action items:
- [Aisha] PR the initial repo with CLI skeleton and one profile (due 2024-11-25) — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/312
- [Marcus] Draft schema proposal and VersionedSummary RFC (due 2024-12-01) — link to confluence: confluence:PD-4321-cust-vpc-simulations
- [Priya] Draft SIEM ingestion test cases and expected mapping to logs pipeline (due 2024-12-10)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and intended to land quickly as a test harness that improves our ability to validate approval gates and forensic UX. Expect several follow-ups: schema tightening, larger corpus generation, and integration with the attestation service.

Raw brainstorming snippets (notes-to-self preserved):
- consider embedding deterministic anomaly triggers so one can fire a "silent-misapply" where manifest says success but netflow shows block
- simulate operator-network-latency for distributed approvals (two-step OK flow)
- think about a tiny DSL for profiles: change:sg add {cidr} -> approval:console-canary -> monitor:flow-drops

References and related docs:
- Confluence: PD-4321-cust-vpc-simulations (design notes)
- Jira: PD-789-change-sim (epic)
- GH: private-deploy PR 312 (starter)

End of doc.
